brand_notes.materials: Two completely different families. (1) TOURING PANNIERS AND TRUNK BAGS: PVC-coated polyester tarpaulin, PD620 body over PS490 gussets. Semi-gloss, stiff, holds a crease; it folds into a few large flat-sided planes rather than draping. Seams are high-frequency WELDED, not sewn - a flat 12-15 mm slightly glossier band with no stitch line and no seam allowance ridge. A mesh that creases like Cordura will read wrong. (2) BIKEPACKING LINE (Seat-Pack, Handlebar-Pack, Frame-Pack, Fork-Pack, Saddle-Bag, Micro-Bag, Gravel-Pack): PU-coated nylon PS21R/PS33, matte, with a fine embossed HEXAGON ripstop grid about 4 mm across on the main panels. Much softer drape, fine wrinkling, contrast bound edges. Never give these two families the same material.
brand_notes.ql21: QL2.1 rail: a rigid black glass-filled-nylon rail bolted horizontally across the BACK panel. Its centreline sits ~20-22% of the bag height down from the top edge and it spans ~82% of the bag width. Both its upper and lower edges are a continuous ladder of teeth so the hooks can be slid to any spacing. Three fixing screws visible: one at each end, one at centre. Two QL2.1 hooks clamp onto that rail, symmetric about the bag centreline, typically at ~28% and ~72% of the bag width (110-160 mm apart). Each hook is a black moulded body about 45 x 35 mm on the panel and standing ~30 mm proud of it, carrying an alloy hook jaw that opens downward/rearward over the rack top tube plus a sprung latch that snaps closed beneath the tube. The bore takes reduction inserts (8 / 10 / 12 mm) for thinner rack tubing; nominal max tube 16 mm. A moulded grab handle ~140 mm wide sits immediately ABOVE the rail; its two legs run down behind the two hooks. Lifting the handle retracts both hook latches at once - it is part of the mount, not just a carry handle. Lower rail hook: on the bag centreline at ~62-68% of the bag height, a dark grey arced backing bracket ~120 mm wide screwed at both ends, with a black hook that slides along the arc and is locked by a central knurled thumbscrew. It reaches back to catch the rack lower stay or vertical leg and is what stops the bag swinging. Bottom bumper: a rigid black arced skid rail bolted across the full width of the bottom of the back panel, ~15 mm deep, three screws, "Made in Germany" moulded into the centre. It stands the bag off the ground and takes the abrasion - model it as a hard lip, not fabric.
brand_notes.mountSystems: QL2.1 - Back-Roller, Back-Roller Plus, Back-Roller Core, Back-Roller XL, Sport-Roller, Sport-Roller Core, Sport-Packer, Bike-Packer, Bike-Packer Plus. QL2.2 (twin separate hook plates plus a steel securing cable, no rail) - Gravel-Pack; also offered on the Back-Roller XL. QLS / Quick-LockS (bolt-on adapter plate, 3x M5 fork bosses) - Fork-Pack. Top-Lock (four clamp jaws on a rigid underframe) - Trunk-Bag and Trunk-Bag RC. Bar-Lock (bar-clamped adapter plate, quick release) - Handlebar-Pack QR. Seat-Lock (saddle-rail clamp plus 22-35 mm seatpost clamp with a rigid slotted arm) - Seat-Pack QR. Tube-Lock (baseplate bolting to top-tube eyelets or held by rubber ladder-straps) - Toptube-Bag and Fuel-Pack. Plain hook-and-loop straps - Seat-Pack, Handlebar-Pack, Handlebar-Pack Flex, Frame-Pack family.
brand_notes.reflectiveSignature: Almost every Ortlieb bag carries the same reflective element: a light-grey 3M PENTAGON-SHIELD patch roughly 90 mm across (smaller on the little bags). On panniers it is on the outboard gusset at mid-height; on the bikepacking bags there are usually two or more on the flanks. Getting this shape right does a lot of work for recognisability.
brand_notes.pairVsSingle: Back-Roller XL, Gravel-Pack (pair listing), Sport-Roller, Sport-Packer, Bike-Packer and Bike-Packer Plus are sold as PAIRS and their headline litres are often quoted doubled. Every capacity_l in this file is the SINGLE bag.
brand_notes.renderPolicy: HEADLINE: for Ortlieb, unlike Tailfin, the published height of a rolltop PANNIER is already the rolled-down ready-to-ride height, and drawing it at the published figure is correct. Do not shrink the Back-Roller family. Proof is both arithmetic and photographic - the Back-Roller boxes out at 1.14x its rated volume (so an unfurled reading is arithmetically impossible), and the near-orthographic elevation back-roller-back-roller-plus-23l-4.jpg measures 785 x 600 px = 1.31 against a published 41.9/32 = 1.309. Sport-Roller and Gravel-Pack box out at 0.79x, which is even more decisive. Only THREE products needed their drawn height cut: Trunk-Bag RC 12L (30 -> 26 cm, box/volume 1.91, confirmed on two orthogonal views), Fork-Pack 4.1L (27.9 -> 25) and Fork-Pack 5.8L (30.5 -> 27), where the studio photos show the roll standing up after a single turn rather than turned down. Ten products carry no render block because their height is genuinely fixed: the four zipped Frame-Packs, the two magnetic-lid top-tube bags, the magnetic-lid Trunk-Bag, and the three flap-lid Packer panniers. SCHEMA GAP: on the roll-at-both-ends Handlebar-Packs and on the Seat-Packs the variable axis is LENGTH, not height - the render block only defines hgt_cm, so len_cm has been added as an extra key on the two 15 L Handlebar-Packs (57.9 -> 48 and 53.1 -> 46, since the published tube is wider than a drop bar). For the Seat-Packs the ridden length is deliberately left un-estimated: the local photo set is studio-only with no on-bike side elevation, and deriving a length from the box/volume ratio would be the back-computation the spec prohibits.
brand_notes.dimensionPolicy: Ortlieb publishes exactly one dimension triple per product on us.ortlieb.com - no min/max ranges anywhere I could find. So the unfurled-plan / minimum-height rule reduces to "use the published figure and say so", which every record does. Where the published figure is manifestly the unfurled one (the roll-at-both-ends Handlebar-Packs, the Seat-Packs) that is called out in dims_note. Four products have a bounding box SMALLER than their claimed volume - Gravel-Pack, Sport-Roller, Sport-Roller Core, Sport-Packer and the Accessory-Pack - which means the published depth is a flat/base measurement; those are flagged rather than silently rewritten.

products.name: Back-Roller
products.dims_raw: Height 16.5 in, Width 12.6 in, Depth 6.7 in (41.9 x 32.0 x 17.0 cm) PER BAG; Volume 20 L PER BAG (the pair listing quotes 40 L); Weight 33.5 oz per bag; Max load 19.8 lb per bag; scope of delivery "2x pannier with QL2.1 mounting system, 2x shoulder strap, 2x set of reduction inserts"
products.dims_note: Single published triple, used as-is; axes verified against the on-bike geometry: 32 cm is the fore-aft run, 17 cm the across-bike depth, 41.9 cm the drop. Box 22.8 L against 20 L (1.14x) - unusually tight, which tells us 41.9 cm is the height with the top ALREADY rolled down, not the unfurled mouth. Volume is 20 L PER BAG even though the product is sold and often quoted as a 40 L pair; capacity_l is the single bag.

geometry.notes: The classic. Outer face is a rounded rectangle: level top, sides falling almost vertically but converging so the bottom is about 88% of the top width, level bottom, large corner radii. The back panel is FLAT and stiff; the outer face domes out. In profile the bag is a slab with one flat side. What makes the current render read as a featureless suitcase is that all the character lives on the surface, not in the silhouette: the roll tube along the top, the V of the shoulder strap across the outer face, the two screwed anchor discs on the centreline, the reflective shield on the gusset, and on the back the rail, two hooks, handle, lower hook and bottom bumper.

closure.hardware: The top hem carries a flat stiffener strip so the mouth stays straight. The top is rolled 2-3 turns toward the OUTER face; a webbing tab at each end of the roll carries a black plastic hook that engages a mating fitting high on the side gusset and is tensioned by a cam. Each of those two roll-end fittings also carries a stamped steel D-ring - those are the shoulder-strap anchors.

straps.material: grey webbing with a moulded slider pad
straps.note: Removable shoulder strap makes the signature V across the OUTER face: it clips to the D-ring at the top rear corner, runs diagonally down and forward, passes through a screwed-on plastic guide on the centreline at ~85% of the bag height, and returns up to a D-ring on a short webbing tab screwed to the centreline at ~15% of the bag height. Both anchor plates are visible black discs with a single central screw - a small but very legible detail on an otherwise blank face.
One at each end of the roll; each carries a plastic hook that engages a fitting on the side gusset and a steel D-ring for the shoulder strap.

details.reflective: a light-grey 3M pentagon-shield patch, roughly 90 mm across, welded to the OUTBOARD side gusset at about mid-height - on the High-Visibility colourway this is joined by a full reflective band round the perimeter of the outer face
details.hardwareColour: all mounting hardware is black glass-filled nylon; only the roll-end D-rings and the QL hook jaws are bright metal
details.backPlate: the whole back panel is stiffened - it is the only flat, unyielding face on the bag and it must not be modelled as draping fabric
details.fabric: PVC-coated polyester tarpaulin (PD620 body / PS490 gussets). Semi-gloss, stiff drape: it creases into a few large flat-sided folds rather than draping in many soft wrinkles, and holds a crease. Gussets are a matte, coarse-woven black. All seams are high-frequency WELDED, so there is no stitch line and no seam allowance ridge - just a flat 12-15 mm welded band, slightly glossier than the panel.
details.note: The tarpaulin is stiff enough that the outer face shows only two or three long flat-sided creases running down from the roll, never a fine wrinkle field.

mount.notes: QL2.1 rail: a rigid black glass-filled-nylon rail bolted horizontally across the BACK panel. Its centreline sits ~20-22% of the bag height down from the top edge and it spans ~82% of the bag width. Both its upper and lower edges are a continuous ladder of teeth so the hooks can be slid to any spacing. Three fixing screws visible: one at each end, one at centre. Two QL2.1 hooks clamp onto that rail, symmetric about the bag centreline, typically at ~28% and ~72% of the bag width (110-160 mm apart). Each hook is a black moulded body about 45 x 35 mm on the panel and standing ~30 mm proud of it, carrying an alloy hook jaw that opens downward/rearward over the rack top tube plus a sprung latch that snaps closed beneath the tube. The bore takes reduction inserts (8 / 10 / 12 mm) for thinner rack tubing; nominal max tube 16 mm. A moulded grab handle ~140 mm wide sits immediately ABOVE the rail; its two legs run down behind the two hooks. Lifting the handle retracts both hook latches at once - it is part of the mount, not just a carry handle. Lower rail hook: on the bag centreline at ~62-68% of the bag height, a dark grey arced backing bracket ~120 mm wide screwed at both ends, with a black hook that slides along the arc and is locked by a central knurled thumbscrew. It reaches back to catch the rack lower stay or vertical leg and is what stops the bag swinging. Bottom bumper: a rigid black arced skid rail bolted across the full width of the bottom of the back panel, ~15 mm deep, three screws, "Made in Germany" moulded into the centre. It stands the bag off the ground and takes the abrasion - model it as a hard lip, not fabric. Handed: the pair mirrors about the bike centreline, so the reflective patch, the roll-end hardware and the shoulder-strap V always face OUTBOARD and the QL rail always faces the wheel. wid is given as +z (drive side); negate it for the non-drive bag. Hangs beside the rear wheel from a rear rack top rail; the hooks carry all the vertical load and the lower hook only resists swing.

render.basis: Ortlieb publish the ROLLED-DOWN height for their panniers, not an unfurled one, so the drawn height equals the published height - this is the opposite of the Tailfin case the amendment cites and a builder must not shrink these. Two independent checks. (1) Arithmetic: 32 x 17 x 41.9 = 22.8 L for a 20 L bag, a ratio of 1.14. If 41.9 cm were the unfurled mouth, the rolled bag would stand about 34 cm and box out at 18.5 L - less than its own rated volume, which is impossible. (2) Measurement: back-roller-back-roller-plus-23l-4.jpg is a near-orthographic elevation of the bag closed with the roll turned down three times and the cam buckles clipped to the side D-rings. Front face measures 785 px tall by 600 px wide = 1.31, against the published 41.9/32 = 1.309. Exact. The same holds across the family: Sport-Roller and Gravel-Pack box out at 0.79 of their rated volume, so their published 37.1 cm cannot possibly be an unfurled figure either.
